chunks: Ali ibn Mahziyar from al-Hasan from Hammam ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "If you have strength, settle the day's prayers during the night."

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.صَلَاةَ النَّهَارِ: The five daily prayers prescribed for the daytime hours

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to 'settle the day's prayers at night' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) encourages the faithful to leverage their physical vitality by performing the five daily prayers during the night hours, a practice known as *taqdim* (early performance) or *jam'* (consolidation). This reflects the Shia emphasis on *salat al-layl* and the spiritual merit of praying when one is fresh, thereby transforming routine obligations into acts of heightened devotion and discipline.
